summary: Zuiryu Nakamura worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Susumu Yamaguchi and Kenryu Tsukinowa. He served as professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University from 1945 and was former director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.
Gyurme tubten nyinje studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.
Pad+ma la studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Édouard Chavannes specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Collège de France, and INALCO under Marie-Jean-Léon d'Hervey de Saint-Denys and Maurice Jametel, later serving as professor at the Collège de France (1893–1918).

A scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Édouard Huber studied under Johann Baptist Schibenegg and Sylvain Lévi at the Sorbonne, Collège de France, and ENLOV. From 1901 to 1905, he was director of the China and Indochina department at EFEO.
Élisée Reclus studied at the Faculté libre de théologie protestante de Montauban (1848–1849) and held a post at the New University of Brussels (~1894–1905).

A scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Benveniste studied at the University of Paris and EPHE under Antoine Meillet, Joseph Vendryes, and Sylvain Lévi. He held chairs at EPHE (1927–1969) and the Collège de France (1937–1969).
Specializing in philosophy, Émile Chartier studied at the Lycée Pierre-Corneille (~1881–1886) and the École Normale Supérieure (~1889–1892).

Émile Chatelain worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1872–1876), later holding posts at the École française de Rome (1876–1877) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1881–1925).

Durkheim worked in religious studies and related fields, studying at the École Normale Supérieure and under Wilhelm Wundt in Leipzig. He held posts at the University of Bordeaux (1887–1902), EPHE (1905), and the Sorbonne as professor (~1902–1917).

Senart specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Munich and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, served as professor at the Collège de France, and was president of the Société Asiatique (1908–1928).

Émile-Louis Burnouf worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and University of Paris under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf, later serving as professor at the University of Nancy (1854–1867) and director of the École française d'Athènes (1867–1875).
Émilie Aussant specializes in Indology and linguistics, having studied under Georges-Jean Pinault. She held an attested post at Paris Diderot University in 2014.

Étienne Balazs, a Sinologist and historian, earned his doctorate under Otto Franke (1923–1930). He was a research director at the CNRS from 1949 and served as professor of Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (~1955–1963).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Lamotte studied at KU Leuven, EPHE, and Collège de France under Louis de La Vallée Poussin, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He taught at KU Leuven (1932–1974) and served as president of UCLouvain (1950–1959).

Quatremère specialized in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (~1800–1807) and held a post at the Collège de France from 1819 to 1857.

Ñāṇavīra Thera, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at Magdalene College, Cambridge, and with traditional teachers Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Pelene Siri Vajiragnana. He served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and the Intelligence Corps (1941–1945).

A Buddhist studies practitioner, Ösel Tendzin studied at Fordham University and under Satchidananda Saraswati and Chögyam Trungpa. He served as executive vice president of Vajradhatu beginning in 1973, later succeeding Trungpa in 1987.
Ülo Valk specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1981–1986), where he held a post around 1995, and has served as an editor for Numen.
